structured.answer: It's worth having. My employer puts in 7.5% and I put in 2.5%, and after 6 years from the first payment I can take all of it out tax-free. Before that I can take it out, but it's taxed, up to 47% the page says, so I don't touch it. Only weird part: the calculator says the keren leaves only 415 ₪ more than a regular securities account, which I don't really get.

stuck.why: After 10 years it says the keren leaves only '415.84 ₪ יותר'. That seemed tiny for something everyone calls a great deal, and I'm not sure if that includes the employer's money.
It's on 12,000 gross. I only know my take-home of 9,500 and not my gross, so I left it as it was.
The minus sign made me think the keren can come out worse, and that scared me a bit.

findings.what: The big result is only '415.84 ₪ יותר' after 10 years. That makes the keren look almost pointless and doesn't clearly say whether the employer's 7.5% is counted.
A range with a minus sign ('342.02–₪') makes it look like the keren can lose to a regular account
Fees in shekels (2,402 ₪) look big next to 466 ₪, which scares me off, but the fee table later just says 'עד 2%'
The salary field wants gross. I only know my net.
A lot of jargon underlined in the text (הפקדה מוטבת, ריאלי, ותק)
Nothing tells me what to do next, like checking which keren HR picked for me
